title: Possible Minds
subtitle: Twenty-Five Ways of Looking at AI
pitch: Brockman asked twenty five scientists and thinkers to respond to Norbert Wiener's 1950 warnings about machines. The answers range from deep worry to calm optimism.

chapters.g: The starting point: The Human Use of Human Beings and its worries about automation and control.
Essays on whether we can keep powerful AI aligned with human values, including Stuart Russell and Max Tegmark.
What intelligence and consciousness mean, and whether machines can have them.
Contributors who think the risks are overblown or that AI will be a great tool.
How AI could reshape politics, work and art.

ideas: Wiener's 1950 warnings still frame today's debate.
Experts disagree deeply about AI risk.
The control problem is taken seriously by leading scientists.
AI raises questions about mind, value and power.

args.a: Many leading thinkers see AI control as a serious problem.
args.c: Others in the same book argue fears are overblown, showing there was no consensus.

args.a: Old ideas from cybernetics still guide us.
args.c: Some say modern machine learning makes Wiener's frame dated.

questions: Which way of looking at AI is closest to yours?
What would Wiener make of the debate?
Which side has gained ground since 2019?

quiz.q: Whose ideas does the book respond to?
quiz.w: His 1950 book on cybernetics and society.

quiz.q: How many ways of looking at AI does the subtitle promise?
